newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares pulled higher by VW, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: German shares pulled higher by VW, seen stable.

text.p: German shares rose in quiet trade on Friday, buoyed by a five percent gain in carmaker Volkswagen AG, but dealers predicted share prices would trade sideways for the rest of the session.
At 0820 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 19.05 points or 0.55 percent at 3,457.14 points in electronic trade shortly before the start of floor trading at 0830 GMT.
Several share traders contacted by Reuters said they had no real explanation for the jump in VW which was the top gainer in the DAX, up 51.90 marks or 4.73 percent at 1,148 marks.
"The big question is why VW is so strong. I've heard it's because of chart technical factors. The volumes look good," said one trader.

Dealers predicted the DAX would move in a range of 3,450 to 3,470, with trading likely to be subdued due to the absence of many players who have taken Friday off for an extended weekend break after Thursday's May Day holiday.
The resounding victory of Britain's Labour Party in the general election, ending 18 years of Conservative rule, had little impact on shares here.
Economists said that while Labour's approach towards Europe would be less hostile than that of the Conservatives, policy would not change much in the foreseeable future.
The main event of the day should be the release of U.S. April payrolls data at 1230 GMT, dealers said, adding that any weakness in the data could push shares prices higher.
